articles.title: SPEC Lime Pixel Confetti
articles.summary: Matte field speckled with tiny hard gloss pops; micro glitter sparkle, low sheen overall. Reads as a gritty digital-noise glitter, a pixelated shimmer that survives farther than most micro textures; no lime colour, it is shine only.
articles.what: Lime pixel confetti with small hard gloss pops across a matte field. Up close: Random square pixels about 8 px each, like an 8-bit mosaic or digital noise, some bright and some dark, scattered across the whole surface with clumps of two or three squares. Strong blocky sparkle inside the highlight on both halves, a bit brighter and higher contrast on metal. From a distance: Reads as a gritty digital-noise glitter, a pixelated shimmer that survives farther than most micro textures; no lime colour, it is shine only. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Source Pattern Plates (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Source Pattern Plates", or search for "SPEC Lime Pixel Confetti".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, sides and roof: broad panels show the noise
Skip small trim: pixels are too big to resolve there
Numbers keep their colour; the pixel noise adds visible grit behind thin numerals, so use large bold numbers.
Clear pixel confetti with medium contrast; blocky sparkle across the highlight
Pairs well with: matte, satin, gloss.
pitfalls: Not lime green paint: spec only, no colour
Not metal flake: elements are square pixels, not irregular flakes
Avoid: too small to read at distance, busy over complex liveries.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.
